title: Freya and the Inheritance
premise: Lena Coldharbour, a nonbinary insurance investigator whose photographic memory has made them both brilliant and isolated, receives two letters after the death of reclusive heiress Freya Vane: one confessing to her murder, the other promising that 'the inheritance is not finished.' As Lena investigates, they discover Freya was their estranged aunt and that Lena is named in her will—deliberately drawn into a family that erased them decades ago. The killer is Freya's archivist, Marta, who has spent years curating the family's records and killing to control which version of history survives. At the anniversary dinner, Lena uses their memory of a doctored photograph to trap Marta in front of the assembled heirs, choosing at last to belong to a found family of their own making rather than the bloodline that discarded them.
about_author: Kestrel Ashgrove is the pen name of a former records clerk who spent eleven years cataloguing other people's unfinished business before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about people who remember too much and are loved too little.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. On the same morning, two letters arrive: a confession to Freya Vane's death signed with no name, and a second note promising 'the inheritance is not finished.' Lena, who files lives away for a living, feels the first crack in their practiced invisibility. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into reluctant curiosity.

chapters.title: The Photograph That Isn't
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Reviewing the estate file, Lena's photographic memory flags a family photograph from 1998 where a child's face has been airbrushed out. The insurer wants the claim closed; Lena wants to know why a dead woman kept a falsified memory framed on her wall. Beat: quiet obsession taking root.

chapters.title: Vane House
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena travels to the coastal estate for the claims assessment and meets the household: brittle nephew Aldous, his anxious wife Corinne, and Marta, the archivist who seems to know Lena's file better than they do. Beat: the uncanny feeling of being expected.

chapters.title: Named in the Will
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Solicitor Devi Raman reveals Freya's will names Lena as beneficiary—a name Freya shouldn't have known. Lena learns Freya was their great-aunt, the sister who vanished from family records the same year the photograph was altered. Beat: vertigo; the past reaching for them.

chapters.title: What Memory Keeps
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Lena's POV. A childhood memory surfaces: a woman on a train platform pressing a brass key into young Lena's hand, saying 'remember me properly.' Lena had filed it as a dream. Now it reads like an instruction. Beat: grief for a protection they never knew existed.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Domain
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Marta catalogs the Vane papers with devotional care, noting with satisfaction that certain pages have already been removed. She observes Lena with interest—not suspicion, but appraisal, as if checking a document against its record. Beat: chilling tenderness toward controlled history.

chapters.title: Aldous Debts
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Aldous begs Lena to expedite the payout; gambling debts have made him desperate, and he half-confesses knowledge of the letters. He becomes the obvious suspect—and Lena lets the obviousness sit uncomfortably. Beat: sympathy tangled with distrust.

chapters.title: Corinne's Version
chapters.summary: Corinne's POV. Corinne privately tells Lena she saw Marta burning papers the night Freya died, then immediately recants, terrified. Her fear reveals the household's true architecture: everyone orbits Marta's version of events. Beat: isolation recognized in another person.

chapters.title: The Brass Key
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The childhood key opens a rented storage unit in town containing Freya's true archive: letters, medical records, and evidence that Freya was slowly poisoned over months. Someone curated a false archive inside the house. Beat: dread—the killer is still editing.

chapters.title: Anniversary Preparations
chapters.summary: Devi's POV. Devi prepares the annual memorial dinner marking Freya's parents' deaths, a Vane tradition where the will will be formally read. Invitations go out; Marta insists on handling seating, menus, and one unexplained addition to the guest list. Beat: ceremony as trap being set.

chapters.title: A Third Letter
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A third letter arrives at Lena's hotel: photographs of Lena's own life—apartments, workplaces, the train platform—proving long surveillance. The message: 'You were always part of this story. Stop pretending otherwise.' Beat: invisibility revealed as an illusion.

chapters.title: The Poison Ledger
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Among Freya's hidden papers, Lena finds a ledger in Freya's hand documenting small doses over eighteen months—and naming her suspected poisoner. The final entry is torn away. Lena memorizes every page before anything can be taken. Beat: resolve hardening into strategy.

chapters.title: Aldous Confesses
chapters.summary: Aldous's POV. Cornered by debt collectors and Lena's questions, Aldous confesses to writing the first letter—he confessed to a murder he didn't commit because blackmail forced him to sign something. The real letter-writer used him as a decoy. Beat: pity; the guilty covering for the truly dangerous.

chapters.title: Marta's History
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena traces Marta's past: hired thirty years ago after a scandal at a national archive involving falsified provenance records. Every Vane family tragedy since—an uncle's suicide, a cousin's disappearance—coincides with documents Marta catalogued. Beat: pattern recognition becoming horror.

chapters.title: The Erased Child
chapters.summary: Freya's letters, read in Lena's POV. Freya's correspondence reveals she discovered Marta had falsified the 1998 photograph to erase a child born out of wedlock—Freya's grandniece, given up to protect the family name. The child was Lena. Beat: belonging and betrayal arriving in the same breath.

chapters.title: Corinne Disappears
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Corinne vanishes after leaving a voicemail: 'She keeps everything. Even us.' Police find the storage unit ransacked—but Lena's memory holds what the thieves came to destroy. Beat: stakes turn personal and mortal.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Marta visits Lena, offering partnership: together they could curate the Vane legacy, decide what deserves to be remembered. She speaks of memory as mercy, deletion as love. Lena understands they are being recruited—or marked. Beat: seduction of complicity.

chapters.title: Setting the Table
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena accepts the anniversary dinner invitation and quietly arranges the board: Devi alerted, Aldous coached, a police contact seated as a 'caterer,' and the original photograph requested for display per Freya's will. Beat: the investigator finally investigating themselves into the open.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. Toasts are raised; Marta presents her curated family history as a slideshow tribute. When the doctored photograph appears, Lena stands and recites, verbatim, the pages only Marta could have destroyed—including the torn ledger entry naming her. Beat: memory deployed as testimony.

chapters.title: Curator's Fall
chapters.summary: Climax, Lena's POV. Marta, cornered before witnesses, calmly explains her philosophy—that families are stories, and stories need editors—before lunging for the fireplace and the last incriminating page. Corinne, alive and hidden in the house, locks the study door from outside. Beat: the keeper of records imprisoned by her own archive.

chapters.title: Reading of the Will
chapters.summary: Devi's POV. Days later, the true will is read: Freya left Lena not money but the choice—keep the estate, or burn the archive and start clean. Lena chooses neither entirely: they donate the truthful records to a public trust and keep only the train-platform photograph, restored. Beat: inheritance redefined.

chapters.title: Remember Me Properly
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Epilogue. Lena hosts an odd, warm dinner—Aldous sober, Corinne laughing, Devi arguing about tea—at the house they almost sold. For the first time, a memory arrives without pain. They write a letter of their own and mail it to no address yet, to whoever comes next. Beat: belonging, chosen and unhurried.
